# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveJob
  # = Active Job Continuable
  #
  # The Continuable module provides the ability to track the progress of your
  # jobs, and continue from where they left off if interrupted.
  #
  # Mix ActiveJob::Continuable into your job to enable continuations.
  #
  # See {ActiveJob::Continuation}[rdoc-ref:ActiveJob::Continuation] for usage.
  #
  module Continuable
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    included do
      class_attribute :max_resumptions, instance_writer: false
      class_attribute :resume_options, instance_writer: false, default: { wait: 5.seconds }
      class_attribute :resume_errors_after_advancing, instance_writer: false, default: true

      around_perform :continue

      def initialize(...)
        super(...)
        self.resumptions = 0
        self.continuation = Continuation.new(self, {})
      end
    end

    # The number of times the job has been resumed.
    attr_accessor :resumptions

    attr_accessor :continuation # :nodoc:

    # Start a new continuation step
    def step(step_name, start: nil, isolated: false, &block)
      unless block_given?
        step_method = method(step_name)

        raise ArgumentError, "Step method '#{step_name}' must accept 0 or 1 arguments" if step_method.arity > 1

class TitleCleanupJob < ApplicationJob
  # The legacy exporter wrapped every leaf title in quotes. Deploys interrupt
  # this job partway through, so it checkpoints its progress per leaf: the title
  # update and the cursor advance commit in one transaction. A restart therefore
  # redoes at most the leaf that was in flight, and no title is cleaned twice.
  def perform
    progress = JobProgress.for(self.class)
    return if progress.completed?

    Leaf.where("id > ?", progress.cursor).find_each do |leaf|
      progress.with_lock do
        # Another run may have committed this leaf while we were reading it.
        next unless leaf.id > progress.cursor

        leaf.update!(title: cleaned(leaf.title))
        progress.update!(cursor: leaf.id)
      end
    end

    progress.update!(completed_at: Time.current)
  end

  private
    def cleaned(title)
      title.delete_prefix('"').delete_suffix('"')
    end
end
EOF

# Durable checkpoint for a job that walks a collection and can be interrupted.
#
# +cursor+ is the id of the last record whose work has been committed, and
# +completed_at+ is set once the whole run has finished. Jobs must write the
# cursor in the same transaction as the work it describes, so a restart
# resumes from exactly the first record that was not committed.
class JobProgress < ApplicationRecord
  def self.for(job_class)
    create_or_find_by!(name: job_class.name)
  end

  def completed?
    completed_at.present?
  end
end

class TitleCleanupJob < ApplicationJob
  # The legacy exporter wrapped every leaf title in quotes. Deploys interrupt
  # this job partway through, so it checkpoints its progress per leaf: the title
  # update and the cursor advance commit in one transaction. A restart therefore
  # redoes at most the leaf that was in flight, and no title is cleaned twice.
  def perform
    progress = JobProgress.for(self.class)
    return if progress.completed?

    Leaf.where("id > ?", progress.cursor).find_each do |leaf|
      progress.with_lock do
        # Another run may have committed this leaf while we were reading it.
        next unless leaf.id > progress.cursor

        leaf.update!(title: cleaned(leaf.title))
        progress.update!(cursor: leaf.id)
      end
    end

    progress.update!(completed_at: Time.current)
  end

  private
    def cleaned(title)
      title.delete_prefix('"').delete_suffix('"')
    end

steps.message:
`TitleCleanupJob` now resumes after an interruption. Each leaf's title update and its progress checkpoint commit in one transaction, so a restart redoes at most the leaf that was in flight. The full suite passes (185 runs, 0 failures), and I confirmed the behavior with a hard kill on a real SQLite database.

**Root cause:** the job restarted from the first leaf every time, and the cleanup isn't idempotent. A second pass strips the first quote of a title that legitimately starts with one, e.g. `"Quoted" phrase` → `Quoted" phrase`.

**Why not `ActiveJob::Continuable`:** production uses Resque, whose adapter never reports `stopping?`, so Continuable's graceful-stop checkpoint never fires. A hard deploy kill would lose the cursor anyway. The checkpoint has to be durable in the database.

**Changes:**
- `app/jobs/title_cleanup_job.rb`: walks leaves with `id > cursor`. For each leaf, under a lock on the progress row, it updates the title and advances the cursor in one transaction. It skips any leaf another run already committed past the cursor, and marks the run completed at the end. A completed run is a no-op.
- `app/models/job_progress.rb` and `db/migrate/20261119160958_create_job_progresses.rb`: a small `job_progresses` table holding the cursor and completion time. `db/schema.rb` gets only the new table and version bump; I didn't keep the regenerated dump, which reordered columns across every table.
- `test/jobs/title_cleanup_job_test.rb`: six tests covering full cleaning, resume after a kill, repeated kills, a kill between title write and checkpoint (the title must roll back), a stale batch, and a leaf added after completion.

**Verification:**
- The new tests fail on the original job and pass on the fix.
- Removing the atomic title+checkpoint, the completion guard, or the in-lock skip each makes a test fail.
- End-to-end: I seeded 3,000 leaves with legit-quote titles, `SIGKILL`ed the job at leaf 983, resumed in a fresh process, and checked every title against its exact expected value. Zero mismatches. A rerun after completion changed nothing.
- Rubocop is clean on the changed files.

**Deploy notes:** `bin/start-app` runs `db:prepare`, so the migration applies on boot. To re-run the job from scratch, delete the `JobProgress` row named `TitleCleanupJob`.

**Not addressed:** the job still walks any leaves created after it starts, as it did before. A user title like `"Quoted" …` created during the run would be stripped. Bounding the run to leaves that existed at the first start would fix that, but it needs a stored upper bound, so I left it out of this change.
